_: Name, description and badge live in src/resources/connectors.json so the console and the browser process cannot disagree about them.

notes: access_type=offline is what produces a refresh token; without it the grant dies in an hour and every scheduled workflow fails overnight.
Google only re-issues a refresh token when the user is re-prompted, so prompt=consent is required on re-authorisation, not just first grant.

gmail.modify covers reading, labelling and saving drafts but NOT sending. Sending needs gmail.send, which is deliberately not requested: a connector that can send is a connector that can send by accident.
These scopes are restricted and need Google verification before the app leaves testing mode.

gmail_create_draft.label: Create a Gmail draft
gmail_create_draft.notes: Saves a draft. Sending a draft is a separate endpoint and a separate scope Flux does not hold.

calendar_create_event.label: Create a calendar event
calendar_create_event.notes: Creating an event notifies attendees, which is an outbound message to other people. Scoped as send, not draft.

rate_limits.note: Per-API quotas, published per service in the Google Cloud console for the project. A 429 means back off and retry with jitter; it is not a permanent failure.

why_prefer_this: Structured errors instead of guessing whether a page silently discarded the action.
Survives the interface redesigns that break DOM-driven automation.
No account-risk exposure, unlike driving a signed-in session.

notes: Endpoints read out of Google's own OIDC discovery document, not from documentation about it.
